title: The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower

sections.name: Hook
lines: cc_hook
In 1925, a man sold the Eiffel Tower. There was just one problem. It wasn't his to sell.
cc_title
This is the true story of Victor Lustig, one of the smoothest con men who ever lived.

sections.name: Paris, 1925
lines: cc_news
Paris, 1925. Lustig reads a newspaper story. The tower is rusting, repairs are costly, and some people say it should come down.
cc_letters
So he forges official government letters, names himself a top official, and invites the city's biggest scrap metal dealers to a secret meeting.

sections.name: The pitch
lines: cc_hotel
They meet at the Hotel de Crillon, one of the grandest hotels in Paris. The tower, he says, will be sold for scrap. Thousands of tons of iron.
cc_mark
But Lustig isn't watching the iron. He's watching the dealers. One of them, André Poisson, is new in town, and desperate to be taken seriously.

sections.name: The bribe
lines: cc_hint
Then Lustig drops a hint. Government officials, he sighs, are so poorly paid. Poisson gets it. He offers a bribe.
cc_proof
And that was the trick. To Poisson, an official asking for a bribe was proof the official was real.
cc_train
Poisson pays for the tower, and the bribe. Within hours, the story goes, Lustig is on a train to Vienna with a suitcase full of cash.

sections.name: The twist
lines: cc_silent
He watches the newspapers for news of the swindle. Nothing. Poisson is too embarrassed to tell anyone.
cc_again
So Lustig comes back and tries the same scam again! This time, a dealer goes to the police, and Lustig slips away to America.

sections.name: The ending
lines: cc_jail
Years later, he was caught for printing fake money, and sent to Alcatraz. He died a prisoner in 1947.
cc_outro
The tower still stands, and it has never been for sale. Would you have fallen for it? Follow for more true crime, animated.
